title: Ryles MT, Pilmanis AA. The initial signs and symptoms of altitude decompression sickness. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1996;67(10):983–989.
note: Armstrong Laboratory archive review of 1,132 exposures and 447 source-defined DCS cases. The overlap with later historical Armstrong/AFRL series is likely. Symptom rows use original counts and retain differences between narrow and broad respiratory definitions.

title: Gray JS, Mahady SCF, Masland RL, Wigodsky HS. Studies on altitude decompression sickness I: Symptomatology. J Aviat Med. 1946;17(4):333–342.
note: Wartime Randolph Field. The printed table reports 852 forced descents in 2,920 seated chamber exposures. The Results text gives 34.3%, which does not match 852/2,920. The underlying symptoms are overlapping and include conditions other than DCS.

title: Henry FM. Altitude pain: a study of individual differences in susceptibility to bends, chokes, and related symptoms. J Aviat Med. 1946;17(1):28–55.
note: Berkeley repeat-flight series of 1,412 person-flights. The 57-man Series A has exact paired symptom and incapacitation counts. Table V percentages use definitions specific to the authors' three historical casualty categories.

title: Kumar KV, Waligora JM, Gilbert JH III. The influence of prior exercise at anaerobic threshold on decompression sickness. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1992;63(10):899–904.
note: Randomized-order crossover with 39 participants and 78 exposures. Control and prior-exercise counts are mathematically recoverable from the exact pooled event count and direction of binary discordant pairs. Analysis preserves shared participants.

title: Rudge FW. The role of ground level oxygen in the treatment of altitude chamber decompression sickness. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1992;63(12):1102–1105.
note: Treatment and consult record series from Brooks AFB, 1989–1991. Includes chamber-only case counts, onset timing and repeat symptoms. Exposure denominators are unavailable. Fifty-six Type I research cases were from the Armstrong Laboratory.

title: Schirmer JU, Workman WT. Menstrual history in altitude chamber trainees. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1992;63(7):616–618.
note: Voluntary survey at 13 USAF units. Of 510 respondents with otherwise usable responses, two developed DCS after completing the card and were excluded from the authors' later 508-response analysis. The 510 denominator is limited to survey respondents.

title: Brooks CJ. Loss of cabin pressure in Canadian forces ejection seat aircraft, 1962–1982. Aviat Space Environ Med. 1984;55(12):1154–1163.
note: Operational aircraft incident series, with 47 serious pressurization losses and two cases counted as DCS. Number of exposed aircrew is not reported. Case 24's affected aircrew role differs between the individual narrative and the Discussion.
